A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transition-path sampling project, retaining the authors, molecular benchmarks, and central discrete training objective despite substantial reframing. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original molecular simulations and TPS-GFN evaluations on Alanine Dipeptide, Polyproline Helix, and Chignolin in Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v4 reports original sampling results on a synthetic double-well system and the three molecular systems, together with component ablations and training curves.

M1.justification: v4 Section 3.3 adds positive scale-based bias forces with Kabsch alignment and replaces the pairwise-distance indicator relaxation with an aligned-coordinate RBF. These substantially change the parameterization and training signal. The squared log-ratio objective, learned scalar, replay buffer, annealing, and variable-length truncation already occur in v3; their reframing alone is not a new algorithm.

E1.justification: v4 adds a two-dimensional double-well transition task with two reaction channels and rejection-sampled reference paths. All three molecular systems remain covered, so the coverage expansion is limited to an additional controlled synthetic setting.

E2.justification: v3 compares against unbiased MD and PIPS. v4 systematically adds steered MD with multiple force constants on every retained molecular benchmark, introducing a substantial classical comparison missing previously. PIPS force and potential variants remain represented; their renamed descriptions do not constitute new comparators.

E3.justification: v4 replaces EPD with aligned heavy-atom RMSD, removes LL/EPCD/EFP, and extends THP and maximum-energy evaluation to Polyproline and Chignolin using handedness and TICA criteria. ETP is renamed ETS with its maximum-energy definition retained. Appendix B changes the reported integrator, Alanine solvent, and training budgets. The new double-well protocol evaluates 1,024 paths. Figures 3–4 have temperature captions conflicting with the main text, leaving those plotting settings uncertain.

E4.justification: v3 provides qualitative path analyses but no component ablations. v4 Section 4.5 adds five ablations covering the loss, control variate, replay, annealing, and variable path lengths, with convergence curves. It also adds an SMD force-constant sensitivity analysis and double-well comparisons against reference transition-state distributions.

E5.justification: v4 Figure 9b newly specifies that training curves average eight different seeds; v3 reports no corresponding repeated-training-run count. Both versions already report plus/minus values in benchmark tables and average molecular metrics over 64 paths. The new seed disclosure does not establish increased repetitions for the retained benchmark tables.

E6.justification: v4 substantially replaces the benchmark results and adds double-well, scaling-model, and ablation entries. Alanine potential-model THP changes from 100.00% in v3 Table 1 to 87.50% in v4 Table 1 under revised settings and criteria. v4 newly reports Chignolin THP of 59.38% for scaling versus 0% for force and potential variants. These are revised-setting findings, not demonstrated same-setting gains or losses.

T1.justification: v3's one-step GFlowNet derivation is replaced by continuous path-measure definitions, a Girsanov-based log-variance derivation, and a derivation connecting the discretized loss to relative trajectory balance in v4 Section 3 and Appendix A. v4 also adds mathematical arguments for positive force alignment and claimed equivariance. This substantially expands the mathematical treatment despite equivalence of the central discrete objectives.

C1.justification: v3 presents a GFlowNet application with a relaxed reward for realistic, diverse CV-free sampling. v4 redefines the contribution around diffusion path samplers, log-variance training, and scale-based equivariant forces for high-dimensional problems. Its headline claims also extend to classical-baseline comparisons and resemblance to reference ensembles.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantial explanations linking performance to replay, annealing, and sparse training signals. Its revised Chignolin analysis emphasizes failure of force/potential variants and the role of scale-based guidance, whereas v3 emphasizes successful folding and advantages of conservative potential-derived forces. The stated limitations concerning larger systems and generalization remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 Appendix B newly specifies MLP depths, activations, Softplus scaling, gradient clipping, heavy-atom alignment, handedness atom selection, and the TICA data-collection and lag settings. It also adds an explicit code link and revises hyperparameter tables. Conversely, v3's GPU hardware and PyTorch implementation disclosures disappear. The net documentation change is substantial.

R1.justification: v4 removes the dedicated GFlowNet and learned-CV discussions and centers its positioning on log-variance diffusion sampling. It adds connections to Nüsken and Richter, Richter and Berner, relative trajectory balance, and concurrent Doob-based sampling, alongside newer trajectory-generation work. This changes the intellectual framing and novelty attribution beyond citation maintenance.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and method narrative are extensively rewritten around TPS-DPS terminology. Experiments are reorganized from separate quantitative/qualitative discussions into system-specific sections and ablations. Appendix A becomes a multipart method derivation, and the training algorithm moves there from the main text.

P2.justification: v4 changes the main text from two columns to one, consolidates benchmark results into a four-system table, and substantially redraws and reorganizes molecular visualizations. It expands the Alanine comparison panels and adds double-well landscapes/distributions, Chignolin TICA plots, ablation curves, and the SMD trade-off plot. These exceed renumbering or numerical table updates.

improvement.justification: v3 lacked controlled component tests and reference-ensemble validation. v4 addresses these central evidential gaps through Figure 9's ablations and eight-seed curves, Figures 2–3's double-well validation, and systematic SMD comparisons. More explicit implementation details further strengthen reproducibility. Removing whole-path likelihood checks and introducing conflicting temperature captions weaken reporting, but the gains in testing sampling fidelity and explaining training choices constitute a substantial overall improvement.
